meaning: The account exists but Supabase requires the user to click the confirmation link before signing in, and they have not yet (or the email never arrived).
causes: 'Confirm email' is enabled in Auth > Providers > Email (the default).
The confirmation email went to spam or was never sent because the built-in email service is heavily rate limited.
The link pointed at localhost or a wrong Site URL, so the click failed.
Test users were created by the app before you set up email.

steps.text: Tell the user what happened: catch this error and show 'Check your inbox to confirm your email' with a resend button.
steps.code:
const { error } = await supabase.auth.resend({ type: 'signup', email,
  options: { emailRedirectTo: `${window.location.origin}/auth/callback` } })

steps.text: Set Auth > URL Configuration > Site URL to your live domain and add your preview/local URLs under Redirect URLs.
For real users, configure custom SMTP (Auth > SMTP settings, e.g. Resend, Postmark, SendGrid). The built-in sender is only meant for testing.
For your own test accounts, confirm them manually in Authentication > Users, or turn off 'Confirm email' only during development.

prompt: Sign in fails with 'Email not confirmed'. Catch this specific Supabase error on the login page and show a friendly message with a 'Resend confirmation email' button that calls supabase.auth.resend({ type: 'signup', email, options: { emailRedirectTo: window.location.origin + '/auth/callback' } }). Make sure signUp also passes emailRedirectTo.

faq.q: Can I just disable email confirmation?
faq.a: Yes, but then anyone can sign up with someone else's email. Fine for prototypes, risky for production.

faq.q: Why are users not getting the email?
faq.a: Usually the default email service limits or spam filtering. Set up custom SMTP.
